classification.difficultyReason: Plot and join coordinates, classify the resulting figures, and select area dimensions; the trapezia require recognising parallel sides and their perpendicular separation, while part e requires recognising perpendicular oblique lines.

content.prompt: Do this exercise on graph paper. Set out the coordinate axes by marking intervals of length 1 unit along the horizontal and vertical axes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Plot the points $O(0,0)$, $A(3,0)$, $C(3,3)$ and $D(0,3)$, and join the points to form the intervals $OA$, $AC$, $CD$ and $DO$. Describe the shape formed and evaluate its area.

answer.worked:
Plot each point using its horizontal coordinate first and vertical coordinate second, then join the intervals shown. All four sides have length $3$ units and adjacent sides meet at right angles, so the shape is a square.

$$\begin{align*}A&=3\times3\\A&=9\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete plotted square on an explicit unit grid. Vertex O is labelled separately from the numeric zero, clear of both coordinate axes.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Plot the points $A(-3,0)$, $B(6,0)$ and $C(0,4)$, and join the points to form the intervals $AB$, $BC$ and $CA$. Describe the shape formed and evaluate its area.

answer.worked:
The joined points form a triangle. Its horizontal base has length $6-(-3)=9$ units, and its perpendicular height is $4$ units.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times9\times4\\A&=18\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete triangle on a unit grid.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Plot the points $A(-4,-3)$, $B(7,-3)$, $C(7,2)$ and $D(-4,5)$, and join the points to form the intervals $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$. Describe the shape formed and evaluate its area.

answer.short:
Trapezium; area $71.5$ square units.

The parallel vertical sides have lengths $8$ and $5$ units and are $11$ units apart.
answer.worked:
The vertical sides $AD$ and $BC$ are parallel, so the shape is a trapezium. Their lengths are $5-(-3)=8$ units and $2-(-3)=5$ units. The perpendicular distance between them is $7-(-4)=11$ units.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{11}{2}(8+5)\\A&=\frac{143}{2}\\A&=71.5\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete trapezium on a unit grid.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Plot the points $A(-4,4)$, $B(1,4)$, and $C(-4,1)$, and join the points to form the intervals $AC$, $CB$, $BA$. Describe the shape formed and evaluate its area.

answer.worked:
$AB$ is horizontal and $AC$ is vertical, so the triangle has a right angle at $A$. Its perpendicular sides have lengths $1-(-4)=5$ units and $4-1=3$ units.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times5\times3\\A&=\frac{15}{2}\\A&=7.5\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete right-angled triangle on a unit grid.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Plot the points $O(0,0)$ and $A(1,2)$, and draw the line passing through these points. Plot the points $B(-2,3)$ and $C(0,2)$, and draw the line passing through these points. Describe the relationship between the lines.

answer.worked: Plot the four points and extend each pair's joining line in both directions. The lines meet at a right angle, so $AO\perp BC$.

spec.description: Two complete lines on a square unit grid, with a coordinate-derived right-angle mark at their intersection. The origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Line OA passes through (0,0) and (1,2); line BC passes through (-2,3) and (0,2). Their intersection is (4/5,8/5), and the lines are perpendicular.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; right-angle mark supplies the conclusion.

children.label: f
children.prompt: Plot the points $A(-1,1)$, $B(3,3)$, $C(7,3)$ and $D(5,1)$, and join the points to form the intervals $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$. Describe the shape formed and evaluate its area.

answer.short:
Trapezium; area $10$ square units.

Its parallel sides have lengths $4$ and $6$ units, with perpendicular height $2$ units.
answer.worked:
$BC$ and $AD$ are horizontal and parallel. Their lengths are $7-3=4$ units and $5-(-1)=6$ units. These opposite sides have different lengths, so the figure is a trapezium rather than a parallelogram. The perpendicular height is $3-1=2$ units.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{2}{2}(4+6)\\A&=10\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete trapezium derived from the printed coordinates, preserving the unequal parallel sides despite the conflicting teacher answer.
